note: Provider-initializer runtime effects the headless brain must NOT run (ADR-0059). Rows name SYMBOLS, never whole files: one initializer routinely mixes brain work with a genuinely renderer-bound effect, and a file-level excuse would silence both. Every reason must say WHY the brain is the wrong host — a physical boundary, or a host-split pair whose brain half is registered in lib/headless/runtimes/. 'Not ported yet' is not a reason; that is debt, and it belongs in the registry instead.

components/providers/initializers/anthro.reason: Polls Anthropic quota through lib/subscription/core/transport, whose whole command family (subscription_get_active, subscription_get_account, ...) is target:client / transports:["internal"] in protocol/companion-commands.json and local-only in protocol/headless-command-dispositions.json. The brain does not read that vault at all: its provider credentials arrive through the claude_set_* arms (R7), which is why lib/headless/runtimes/initializers.ts already excludes subscription-initializer for the same reason. Exposing quota probing to the brain is a subscription-vault decision, not a wiring one.

components/providers/initializers/code-a.reason: The tracker persists through lib/code-adoption/client.ts, whose code_adoption_turn_begin / code_adoption_turn_end are target:client, capability:client.local, transports:["internal"] in the command manifest and local-only in the dispositions ledger — write attribution is measured against the local working tree the desktop edits. Wiring the brain to it would first require reclassifying those two commands, which is a protocol decision (D7 makes the manifest authoritative), not a registration.

components/providers/initializers/codex-.reason: The Codex half of the same decision as anthropic-usage-scheduler-initializer: it resolves the active account through subscription_get_active, which is target:client / internal-transport and local-only in the dispositions ledger. The brain's Codex credentials come from the server secret store via claude_set_*, not from the interactive desktop vault this loop probes.

components/providers/initializers/deferr.reason: The renderer half of ADR-0125 durable work submission: it drains the browser-local queue of work this client originated. The brain is the receiving authority, not a submitter, and runs the server half — registered as `work-submission-outbox` in lib/headless/runtimes/initializers.ts. Running both in one process would have the brain drain its own inbox back into itself.

components/providers/initializers/issue-.reason: Registers the `issue.open` notification command, whose whole body is a Next App Router `router.push`. Navigation is an act on a UI surface the brain does not have; the paired device that RECEIVES the notification installs this command in its own renderer. The other eight effects in this initializer are brain work and are registered as `issue-tracker` in lib/headless/runtimes/issue-tracker.ts.

components/providers/initializers/manage.reason: The Tauri-event-bound entry point; the brain uses the sibling attachManagedIdeBrokerTransport (lib/plugin/ide/broker-runtime.ts:1184) with the companion transport plus content upload/redeem, registered as `managed-ide-broker` in lib/headless/runtimes/managed-ide-broker.ts. One subsystem, two host-specific attach points — not a gap.

components/providers/initializers/remote.reason: The CLIENT side of `notification://remote` — it ingests frames a headless server publishes into this device's Notification Center. The brain is the publisher (lib/notifications/runtime.ts -> remote_notification_publish) and must not subscribe to itself. Already recorded in the roster doc at lib/headless/runtimes/index.ts.

components/providers/initializers/select.reason: Reads the OS-level text selection through the desktop selection-perception bus (ADR-0093/0095). Desktop selection awareness is one of ADR-0059 D7's recorded physical boundaries: there is no OS selection to observe in a container.
Restores the always-on-top native selection-toolbar window (ADR-0093). A recorded physical boundary in ADR-0059 D7 — the brain has no window server to place an overlay on.

components/providers/initializers/sessio.reason: Owns the OS filesystem watch over desktop external-agent history roots. Its session_import_watch_start / session_import_watch_stop commands are target:client, capability:client.local, transports:["internal"] in protocol/companion-commands.json and local-only in protocol/headless-command-dispositions.json. A brain has no Tauri event source or those per-user desktop history paths to watch.

components/providers/initializers/webvie.reason: Proves the Tauri WebView is still painting so the watchdog can recover a wedged renderer. A headless brain has no WebView; its liveness is the supervisor's ready probe and /healthz in cognia-server, which is a different mechanism, not a missing port of this one.

components/providers/initializers/worker.reason: The desktop half attaches a @tauri-apps/api/core Channel to companion_worker_attach_channel. The brain half is the bridge-owned WorkerRpcPool created only after the authenticated bridge connects in cli/src/serve/serve-command.ts, where installRemoteWorkerRuntime is paired with bridge and pool teardown. lib/headless/runtimes/index.ts records this dependency-bound bootstrap exception; a registry import cannot construct that live bridge channel.
